_comment: Coverage matrix for the shared Carve spec corpus (spec/tests/corpus/*.crv). Every NN-slug base category must appear in covered or skip; the coverage-matrix test fails otherwise so a new spec category forces a classify decision. covered = grammar parses every file in the category with no ERROR/MISSING node. skip = at least one file currently produces an ERROR/MISSING node; reason records the unmodeled construct (a grammar gap to surface, not to hack around). A skip key is a CATEGORY (NN-slug) or a single EXAMPLE (NN-slug-2) — use the example form when the rest of the category parses cleanly, so one gap does not drop assertion for its siblings. A key equal to a category name is read as the CATEGORY, so the first example of a category cannot be skipped on its own.

skip.an-attribute-name-admits-no-colon-3: a table row whose trailing attribute block carries an INVALID name (`| a | b |{.a:b}` - a class may not contain a colon) parses to ERROR. The engines make the whole line a paragraph, because the block is not an attribute block at all; this grammar commits to the row on the pipes and has no route back. The category's other two examples parse cleanly, so only this one is skipped.
skip.a-blank-line-holds-spaces-and-tabs-and-n: a paragraph whose interior lines hold a single vertical tab, form feed, NEL (U+0085), LS (U+2028) or PS (U+2029) and nothing else parses to ERROR. PART 9 makes a line blank only when it holds spaces and tabs, so each of these is CONTENT and the paragraph runs through them; this grammar has no line-content route for a line whose only character is one of them. The category's other examples parse cleanly.
skip.trailing-whitespace-on-a-content-line-is: content lines ending in NBSP, ZWSP, BOM, U+2000 or a form feed parse to ERROR. Only the ASCII space and tab are dropped as trailing whitespace; every other spelling is content the renderer keeps, and this grammar's line-content rule does not admit them in that position. The category's other examples parse cleanly.
skip.a-quoted-attribute-value-stops-at-the-ne: a quoted attribute value carrying a newline (`{k="a` / `b"}`) parses to ERROR. The corpus pins it as literal text - the inline block does not span lines - but this grammar commits to an attribute block on the opening brace and has no route back to a paragraph when the value never closes on its line. Same class as an-attribute-name-admits-no-colon-3. The category's other examples parse cleanly.

an-unresolved-reference-image-takes-no-c.reason: `![a][nope]` + `^ cap` is one paragraph: the reference does not resolve, so the image is literal text and the `^` line is literal with it. Whether it resolves depends on the DEFINITIONS in the document, which a context-free grammar does not have - so the caption is built here and cannot be declined without a symbol table. The renderer decides correctly; highlighting a caption that the language declines is the cost.

colon-fence-metadata-slots-must-be-a-spa.reason: the fence opener's metadata slots take exactly one space, so a TAB anywhere in them (after the type word, before or after a quoted title, before a label) makes the whole line prose and the block never opens. This grammar's scanner still opens the fence: its separator test admits a whitespace RUN rather than one literal space. Unlike the other entry here this IS declinable - it needs no symbol table, only a narrower separator - so it is a scanner fix waiting on tree-sitter-carve#160, not a permanent cost. Recorded rather than fixed in the corpus bump that surfaced it, so the bump is not blocked on a scanner change. Spec side: markup-carve/carve#907 and markup-carve/carve#905.

reference-link-5.reason: the reference definition is anchored at end of line and its metadata slots take exactly one space, so `[a]: /u zzz`, `[a]: /u<TAB>{.c}` and `[r]: a b c` are PARAGRAPHS - the line is not a definition at all and every character of it is visible. This grammar still builds a link_reference_definition, which renders nothing, so the fixture's visible text has no node behind it. Declinable without a symbol table: it needs the trailing-content and separator tests the spec now states. Tracked in tree-sitter-carve#160. Spec side: markup-carve/carve#905 and markup-carve/carve#907.

a-fence-opened-on-a-list-marker-line-bod.reason: a code fence opened on a list MARKER line with its body BELOW the item's content column: the item closes with an EMPTY code block and the residue re-parses at document level (markup-carve/carve#646). This grammar builds no code_block for the shape at all. Its scanner commits the fence to the item and has no route to close it at the container boundary. Tracked in tree-sitter-carve#160.

a-frontmatter-opener-takes-exactly-one-s.reason: the OPENER half of this document is fixed: `---  yaml` is no longer read as frontmatter, because the separator is exactly one space. What remains is a different, pre-existing defect that this document happens to also contain - the `---` line BELOW the paragraph is a thematic break in every engine and folds into the paragraph as an em dash here. That is the same gap already recorded for paragraph-interruption-3, so it is one defect with two documents rather than a frontmatter question.

\"-\" + \"---\".reason: a `---` after a content-less marker errors; carve-js renders a paragraph then a thematic break (tree-sitter-carve#96)

a-footnote-body-s-last-block-when-it-is-.spellings: the cr spelling(s) parse to a different tree than lf
a-footnote-body-s-last-block-when-it-is-.reason: a lone carriage return still changes this document's tree. The scanner now treats all three spellings of `newline` as terminators, and 428 of 672 corpus documents that diverged before this do not any more, but these are the remainder: every one of them is a REFERENCE DEFINITION, an ATTRIBUTE BLOCK or a trailing block inside a list item - constructs whose probes read a column, and tree-sitter advances the row and resets the column on '\n' and on nothing else (`lib/src/lexer.c`), so a scanner-maintained base carries them and does not carry every probe that reads one. tree-sitter-carve#143. The same mechanism has one reachable shape outside the corpus: `comment_line` in grammar.js consumes its own terminator in the internal lexer, so a comment line ended by a lone '\r' strands the base for an indented construct below it.

The scanner now treats all three spellings of `newline` as terminators, and 428 of 672 corpus documents that diverged before this do not any more, but these are the remainder: every one of them is a REFERENCE DEFINITION, an ATTRIBUTE BLOCK or a trailing block inside a list item - constructs whose probes read a column, and tree-sitter advances the row and resets the column on '\n' and on nothing else (`lib/src/lexer.c`), so a scanner-maintained base carries them and does not carry every probe that reads one. tree-sitter-carve#143. The same mechanism has one reachable shape outside the corpus: `comment_line` in grammar.js consumes its own terminator in the internal lexer, so a comment line ended by a lone '\r' strands the base for an indented construct below it.
